newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma military eases blockade near Suu Kyi's home.
newsitem.headline: Burma military eases blockade near Suu Kyi's home.

text.p: Burmese authorities have relaxed security around the home of democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi after foiling her party's plans to hold a congress there, sources in Rangoon said on Thursday.
Riot police and barbed wire barricades set up near Suu Kyi's lakeside residence to thwart the planned two-day meeting on Monday have been removed.

"There is one checkpoint and a number of security forces are stationed at an intersection about 0.5 km (0.3 mile) from her house," an aide to the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate said. "The situation in general is calm."
Although there were no barricades, authorities had erected "no entry" road signs to block access to her house.
Only 10 executive committee members of her National League for Democracy (NLD) were allowed entry on Monday.

The NLD had hoped to bring together several hundred of its members and elected members of parliament to mark the anniversary of its 1990 landslide election victory, which was never recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).

The NLD says the SLORC has detained up to 316 party members, including about 50 members of parliament, nationwide to prevent the meeting. It was unknown on Thursday if any had been released and there was no official comment on the matter.
The government denies charges it has detained party members and has asked the NLD to prove its claims.
The Suu Kyi aide said that NLD executive members had met at the party headquarters in Rangoon on Thursday without any intervention by security forces.
Suu Kyi, who is recovering from a recent stomach illness, did not attend. "She is fine, but her doctor told her to rest," the aide said.
